content.text: By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
Describe the main ways humans impact ecosystems
Explain the causes and effects of pollution
Describe habitat destruction and its consequences
Understand climate change and its effects on ecosystems
Humans have significant impacts on ecosystems worldwide. Our activities cause
. Understanding these impacts is essential for developing solutions and protecting biodiversity.
Fish and other organisms die (dead zone)
Build-up of substances in one organism
More greenhouse gases trap more heat
Non-native species that harm native ecosystems
Species whose presence indicates environmental quality
Climate change only means warmer weather
It causes more extreme and unpredictable weather
Pollutants can travel globally (e.g., acid rain, plastics)
Species can easily adapt to rapid changes
Many species cannot adapt fast enough
Small actions don't make a difference
Collective small actions have significant impact
Release of harmful substances into environment
Build-up of substances in an organism
Long-term change in global climate patterns
Humans impact ecosystems through pollution, habitat destruction, overexploitation, and climate change
Air pollution causes acid rain and climate change
Bioaccumulation and biomagnification concentrate toxins in top predators
Deforestation causes habitat loss, climate change, and soil erosion
Climate change affects temperatures, weather, and species distribution
Invasive species outcompete natives and disrupt ecosystems
